content.title: The Chris brown and Usher tour is here! The Usher and Chris brown tour fans have been dreaming of is a reality. Chris brown made it official on his socials today, as did Usher who posted the same teaser trailer for the Raymond and Brown tour leaving fans with one major question what are the Chris brown and ushers tour dates? The Usher Chris brown Tour announcement stole the music news cycle’s headlines on Day 1 of Coachella 2026. If we’re being honest, the Chris brown and Usher tour 2026 might be the biggest concert news of the year. For years, an Usher Chris brown tour was just  fantasy. Now the Chris brown usher tour is happening. While there is no word yet on usher and Chris brown tour dates, we do know usher and Chris brown tour 2026 dates are happening. Usher and Chris brown are two of the biggest r&b icons of the 21st century. Chris brown tour 2026 dates were already highly anticipated, but now that Chris brown and usher have linked up for the r&b tour, it’s no longer a Chris brown tour it’s a usher Chris brown tour and its being called the Raymond and brown tour featuring Chris brown usher and maybe other acts to be announced at a later time. Chris brown Tour dates 2026 was already a hot topic, but an usher and Chris brown concert have been what R&B fans have wanted for years. They now don’t have to dream as Chris brown usher tour 2026 is just months away. Chris brown and Usher have a long history together. Chris Brown’s mom saw Chris brown dancing to Usher’s My Way and knew Chris brown was special. Usher and Chris brown actually met in the 2000s before collaborating on Chris Brown’s New Flame remix in 2014 and again in 2025 on Chris Brown’s It Depends which samples Usher’s Nice & Slow. Usher also appeared at the Breezy Bowl in 2025 in Atlanta. Are you buying tickets for the Chris brown and Usher tour? Let’s talk about it. | Kevan Kenney | Facebook

The Usher and Chris brown tour fans have been dreaming of is…See moreCommentsMost relevant Kimica Caresmisinfo1wGiavonni Campbell1wView more comments2 of 8Related ReelsKevan Kenney 336Kevan Kenney 304Kevan Kenney 300Kevan Kenney 1.1KKevan Kenney 282Kevan Kenney 248Kevan Kenney 656KKevan Kenney 217Kevan Kenney 327Kevan Kenney 487Kevan Kenney 211Kevan Kenney 666Related Videos2:26Hip Hop has come under scrutiny lately as Hip Hop was absent from the Billboard Top 40 for the first time since Biz Markie was putting out Hip Hop records. Is Hip Hop’s absence from the Billboard Top 40 Hip Hop’s own fault for attacking Hip Hop’s biggest hitmaker in Drake? Instead of blaming Kendrick Lamar or blaming mumble rap for Hip Hop’s decline, let’s take a look at the natural life cycles of music genres historically and figure out where Hip Hop is within the Hip Hop life cycle right now. Hip Hop dominated the Billboard Top 40 for decades and Hip Hop shaped pop culture more than any other genre since Hip Hop went mainstream. But Hip Hop being absent from the Billboard Top 40 is a wake up call for Hip Hop fans and Hip Hop artists. Drake was Hip Hop’s biggest hitmaker and Hip Hop turning on Drake during the Drake and Kendrick Lamar beef might have hurt Hip Hop more than Hip Hop fans realized at the time. Kendrick Lamar won the Drake and Kendrick Lamar beef but Hip Hop as a genre lost commercial momentum on the Billboard Top 40 after the Drake and Kendrick Lamar beef ended. Mumble rap gets blamed for Hip Hop’s Billboard Top 40 decline but mumble rap is just one small part of the Hip Hop story. Historically every genre goes through cycles. Rock dominated the Billboard Top 40 for decades before Rock faded from the Billboard Top 40. Disco dominated the Billboard Top 40 before Disco collapsed. Country had Country’s Billboard Top 40 moment before Country faded too. Hip Hop being absent from the Billboard Top 40 is not the end of Hip Hop but Hip Hop absolutely needs to evolve if Hip Hop wants to return to the Billboard Top 40. Biz Markie was putting out Hip Hop records when Hip Hop was still fighting to be taken seriously and now Hip Hop is in a completely different place. The question is whether Hip Hop can reinvent Hip Hop or whether Hip Hop will keep cannibalizing Hip Hop’s biggest stars like Drake. The Hip Hop life cycle is real and Hip Hop fans need to pay attention to where Hip Hop is heading in 2026.Kevan Kenney3K views · 1d ago1:49In 1994 the biggest rock hit wasnt by nirvana, smashing pumpkins, goo goo dolls, Red Hot Chili Peppers, stone temple pilots, or soundgardn or Pearl Jam. The biggest rock hit of 1994 belonged to a band who owed it all to a toiler paper roll. In 1989, a kid named ed wrote a song with his little brother and wound up putting it on a demo compilation in 1993, that song wound up getting played on Atlanta college radio stations and Orlando rock radio stations. The song whose chorus featured ed singing into a toilet paper roll got so much buzz in 1994, Atlantic records signed Ed Roland and his band Collective Soul to a record deal and the toilet paper roll song now known as Shine by Collective Soul hit no 1 on the Billboard rock charts for eight straight weeks in 1994 and got all the way to no. 11 on the billboard hot 100. What’s even craziest for Ed Roland and Collective Soul is Dolly Parton covers the collective soul song shine in 2001 and wins a grammy for her cover of collective soul’s shine. Pretty wild, right? Do you have any 90s nostalgia memories of this 90s rock and grunge classic? Was 2016 as lit as everyone remembers 2016 being? Is the 2016 nostalgia valid or is the 2016 trend overblown? Whether you loved the 2016 aesthetic or hate the 2016 trend, these 2016 songs are for sure 2016 tracks you have not thought about since 2016. Remember Kent Jones? Kent Jones had the DJ Khaled produced 2016 hit Don’t Mind which was everywhere in 2016. What about Kylie Jenner and Terror Jr? Terror Jr made 3 Strikes for Kylie Jenner’s lip kit commercial in 2016 and Terror Jr blew up overnight. Remember Lukas Graham and 7 Years? Lukas Graham’s 7 Years was one of the biggest 2016 songs and 7 Years was everywhere in 2016. What about Desiigner and Panda? Desiigner’s Panda was a massive 2016 hit and Panda even got sampled by Kanye West on Pt 2 from The Life of Pablo in 2016. What about Ruth B and Lost Boy? Ruth B’s Lost Boy was that dreamy 2016 song everyone had on their 2016 playlist. The 2016 trend is bringing back so many 2016 memories of 2016 songs nobody has thought about in years. Kent Jones, Terror Jr, Lukas Graham, Desiigner and Ruth B all had their biggest moments in 2016 and then 2016 ended and these 2016 artists kind of faded from the mainstream. The 2016 aesthetic was so specific with the 2016 fashion, the 2016 slang and the 2016 songs that defined 2016. If the 2016 trend keeps going we might see more 2016 forgotten songs make a comeback the same way 2000s songs have been making a comeback recently. 2016 really was a special year for pop music and hip hop and the 2016 songs above prove just how stacked 2016 was. The 2016 nostalgia hits different when you actually revisit these 2016 tracks and realize how much 2016 music shaped the 2016 aesthetic everyone is obsessed with right now. If you can think of any 2016 forgotten songs or 2016 hits that deserve to come back with the 2016 trend, LMK in the comments which 2016 songs you want to hear next!Kevan Kenney5.8K views · 3d ago1:3950 Cent scored a billion streams with Many Men but Many Men was never supposed to be 50 Cent’s song to begin with. Darrell Digga Branch made the Many Men beat back in 1999 with the intention of giving the beat to Dipset for Dipset’s debut album. Darrell Digga Branch was working with Camron, Jay Z and JLO at the time so Darrell Branch had the connections to get the beat placed. Dipset never ended up doing anything with the Many Men beat so then the Many Men beat went to Nas. Nas was fresh off Nas’s beef with Jay Z at the time and Nas was working on Nas’s album God’s Son which already had hits like I Can and Made You Look. Nas eventually fell out of love with the Many Men beat and so the Many Men beat eventually wound up with 50 Cent who put Many Men on 50 Cent’s debut album Get Rich or Die Tryin in 2003. 50 Cent had bigger hits on Get Rich or Die Tryin like Wanksta, In Da Club and 21 Questions but Many Men became 50 Cent’s origin story and one of 50 Cent’s biggest songs today. Many Men tells the story of 50 Cent getting shot 9 times and surviving, which is why Many Men resonates so deeply with 50 Cent fans. The Many Men beat traveling from Darrell Digga Branch to Dipset to Nas to 50 Cent is one of hip hop’s most fascinating beat journeys. Imagine if Dipset had used the Many Men beat, or if Nas had kept Many Men for God’s Son. 50 Cent’s career and 50 Cent’s legacy might look completely different today. Many Men sampling Tony Bennett’s “The Gentle Rain” gave Many Men that haunting quality that made Many Men timeless. Darrell Digga Branch deserves way more credit for crafting the Many Men beat that became 50 Cent’s signature song. The story of Many Men proves that sometimes the biggest hits in hip hop history almost never happened. 50 Cent got lucky that Dipset passed and Nas passed on Many Men. Many Men is 50 Cent forever.Kevan Kenney12K views · 4d ago1:47Did you know there’s a Coachella movie? Like a real movie. 2 hours long. Was in theaters. The Coachella movie dropped back in 2006 and if you’ve never seen it but actively watching Coachella 2026, you need to watch this early 2000s time capsule immediately. Coachella can be traced back to the band Pearl Jam, not because they played it, because they wouldn’t play anywhere! Pearl Jam boycotted Ticketmaster in the mid 1990s and in 1993, a guy named Paul Tollett came to the rescue and booked Pearl Jam out in the middle of nowhere, the literal desert at a polo club, the Pearl Jam concert drew 25,000 people and Paul TOllett got an idea - 6 years later in 1999, Coachella as born. The first Coachella in 1999 was headlined by Beck, Rage Against The Machine and Tool. Tickets were 50 bucks. Water and parking was free. The first Coachella lost almost a million dollars. The first Coachella went so bad, they didn’t even do it the next year. Fast forward to 2006 and Coachella had a filmmaker filming the Coachella festival for its first half decade and that footage became the Coachella movie in 2006. It features 2000s Coachella favorites like Red Hot Chili Peppers, Flaming Lips, Beck, White Stripes, Bjork and others. Coachella has changed a lot over the years, as anything in life does but if you only know Coachella as the Justin Bieber Coachella Bieberchella takeover or Sabrina Carpenter Coachella or the Karol G Coachella, this 2006 Coachella movie is a great watch to show just how far the Coachella festival has come.Kevan Kenney2.2K views · 5d ago1:48In 2007 Tpain scored the biggest hit of his career to date alongside Yung Joc on Buy U A Drank. It was a bizarre millennial trend that remains a mystery today. Don’t like Snoop Dogg? Ludacris? Joe Budden? Beat them all up in Def Jam Vendetta or Def Jam Fight for NY? Got a problem with Fabolous? Box him in EA Sports Fight Night Round 2. This trend of beating up celebrities goes way deeper. In 1994, Shaquille Oneil, yes SHAQ himself may have started the 90s trend of beating up celebrities in video games when Shaq came out with Shaq Fu a fighting game for the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis. Then in 1995, there was Rap Jam which was a street basketball game featuring Coolio, Queen Latifah, House of Pain, Flava Flav, Public Enemy, Everlasting, DJ Lethal, Onyx, LL Cool J and more. Remember Wu Tang Shaolin Style for Playstation in 1999? That 90s video game even came with a secret cheat code to unlock the uncensored version of Wu Tang Shaolin Style for Playstation back in 1999. In the 2000s, these games were everywhere. Remember how much people hated Limp Bizkit and Fred Durst in 2001? In games like Fight Club of XBOX and Playstation 2, or WWF Raw or WWF Smackdown Just Bring It you could literally fight and wrestle Fred Durst as a playable character. If you grew up on MTV, you probably remember celebrity death match. Celebrity Deathmatch had a game! You could fight as Busta Rhymes, Anna Nicole Smith, Marilyn Manson, Tommy Lee and tons more. Def Jam Vendetta and Def Jam Fight for NY are definitely still king. You could fight as everybody from Fat Joe to Dmx and back. Did you play any of the 2000s video games or 90s video games?
